messages:
jessica: Heads up — since ~09:12 UTC we're seeing GPU node provisioning failures in ap-southeast-1. Errors look like KMS auth denied followed by SG reject on the keystore path. nodes stuck in PROVISIONING state :frowning:
max: I saw that, warm-pool drains too. any quick logs? 
jessica: Logs show repeated TCP RSTs to the keystore proxy IP and a couple 403 KMS responses. snippet:
```
2026-03-19T09:11:34Z node-xyz kubelet: keystore auth failed: KMS: AccessDenied
network: tcp 10.40.12.45:443 -> 10.48.5.12:32000 RST
```
raghav: Looks like a recently applied outbound SG deny (rule id sg-0f1e2d), maybe the egress hardening from last week. @tina did we tighten the egress carveout? 
tina: yep, applied egress deny to lock down S3/DB subnets. That rule accidentally matched the keystore CIDR (10.48.0.0/16). I can revert but it will open more than we'd like. 
chris: Reverting temporarily sounds fine if we disable 10.48/16 full access and instead allow only keystore proxy IPs + regional KMS endpoints. Can we list the proxy IPs? 
jessica: proxy pool IPs: 10.48.5.12, 10.48.5.13, 10.48.5.14. Proposed SG change:
```
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.48.5.12/32
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.48.5.13/32
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-0abc1234 --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.48.5.14/32
```
max: That would be minimal. Also we still have the KMS AccessDenied; roles for the new GPU instances might be missing kms:Decrypt on the keystore CMK.
raghav: I checked the instance profile used by the autoscaler: it references role arn:aws:iam::111222333:role/redwood-node-provisioner. The inline policy doesn't include kms:Decrypt for alias/aws/redwood-keystore. 
tina: Oops — that happened during the role hardening patch last week. I can add a scoped policy quickly:
```
{
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:111222333:key/abcd-ef01-2345"
}
```
chris: +1. Add that and revert the SG deny for the three proxy IPs. We'll monitor provisioning. 
ops-bot: deploybot triggered: infra-change /sg-update 1712349999 by tina queued for ap-southeast-1
deploybot: rollout started: sg-0abc1234 update -> applied 2/3, waiting approval for last rule
tina: applying last rule now, adding IAM policy to role as well. 
jessica: after the SG tweak and role update we saw provisioning resume at 09:24 UTC — queued warm nodes transitioned to READY. thanks. 
max: one follow-up: our audit log ingestion spiked because we were sampling at 100% during the event (for troubleshooting). Previewed cost for March looks +18% on CloudWatch ingestion. Suggest dropping sampling to 20% for non-prod and keep full for prod for 24h. Thoughts? 
raghav: agree. Also propose retention for debug traces in ap-southeast to 7 days (was 30) until traffic normalizes. We'll keep key audit entries (keystore/kms) at full fidelity. 
chris: fine with temporary retention reduction. Please file a PR with the change and tag @security-review. 
jessica: filing now — PR #4827. Patch includes SG updates, IAM policy, and audit sampling/retention tweaks. I'll link to the runbook excerpt in the PR. 
max: postmortem action items:
- tina: add unit test to egress rule deploy pipeline to detect keystore CIDR overlaps
- raghav: ensure node role has kms:Decrypt in baseline template
- jessica: run warm-pool smoke nightly for ap-southeast
chris: set a 48h check on costs and revert retention once stable. 
jessica: thanks team :thumbsup: closing thread unless anyone sees residual errors.
max: seeing a couple of 503s but they look unrelated, open new thread if persists.
